therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: postprandial glucose regulation and appetite suppression
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: insulin-using patients with Type 1 or Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Incidence and annual event rate of Patient-Ascertained Severe Hypoglycemia (PASH) during the adjustment period (0-3 months)

results.effect_size: PASH incidence: T1D 4.8%, T2D 2.8% (adjustment period); annual event rate: T1D 0.3255, T2D 0.1941 events/patient-year
biomarker_changes: HbA1c change at 3 months: T1D -0.12%, T2D -0.33%
HbA1c change at 6 months: T1D -0.26%, T2D -0.44%
Body weight change at 3 months: T1D -1.95 kg, T2D -1.94 kg
Body weight change at 6 months: T1D -2.77 kg, T2D -1.98 kg
subgroup_findings: PASH incidence decreased from adjustment (T1D 4.8%, T2D 2.8%) to steady state (T1D 1.8%, T2D 0.3%) periods
MASH incidence during adjustment period: T1D 1.8%, T2D 0.4%
MASH incidence during steady state: T1D 0.8%, T2D 0.3%
Annual PASH event rate decreased from adjustment to steady state in both T1D (0.3255 to 0.0844) and T2D (0.1941 to 0.0248)
safety_signals: Severe hypoglycemia (PASH) occurred in 4.8% of T1D and 2.8% of T2D patients during adjustment period
Medically assisted severe hypoglycemia (MASH) occurred in 1.8% of T1D and 0.4% of T2D patients during adjustment period
Hypoglycemia risk decreased substantially in steady state period compared to adjustment period

dose_info.schedule: subcutaneous injection prior to each major meal

context.indication: Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in insulin-using patients
